sanskrit: tiryagyonivadhaṃ kṛtvā drumāṃś chittvetarān bahūn trirātraṃ vāyubhakṣaḥ syāt karma ca prathayen naraḥ
english: Having slain a creature of the animal kingdom, or having felled many other sorts of trees, a man should subsist on air alone for three nights and openly proclaim what he has done.

sanskrit: agamyāgamane rājan prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate ārdravastreṇa ṣaṇmāsaṃ vihāryaṃ bhasmaśāyinā
english: For approaching a woman one may not lawfully approach, O king, this penance is ordained: for six months he must go about clad in wet garments and sleep upon ashes.

sanskrit: eṣa eva tu sarveṣām akāryāṇāṃ vidhir bhavet brāhmaṇoktena vidhinā dṛṣṭāntāgamahetubhiḥ
english: This same rule applies to all forbidden deeds, by the procedure declared by the Brāhmaṇas, grounded in precedent, scripture, and reasoning.

sanskrit: sāvitrīm apy adhīyānaḥ śucau deśe mitāśanaḥ ahiṃsro 'mandako 'jalpan mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
english: Even by reciting the Sāvitrī in a clean place, eating sparingly, doing no harm, neither dull nor given to idle chatter, a man is freed from all his sins.

sanskrit: ahaḥsu satataṃ tiṣṭhed abhyākāśaṃ niśi svapet trir ahnas trir niśāyāś ca savāsā jalam āviśet
english: By day he should remain ever standing under the open sky, by night he should sleep beneath it, and three times by day and three times by night he should enter the water with his garments on.

sanskrit: strīśūdrapatitāṃś cāpi nābhibhāṣed vratānvitaḥ pāpāny ajñānataḥ kṛtvā mucyed evaṃvrato dvijaḥ
english: While bound by this vow he should not speak with women, Śūdras, or the fallen; having committed sins through ignorance, the twice-born man so vowed is set free.

sanskrit: śubhāśubhaphalaṃ pretya labhate bhūtasākṣikaḥ atiricyet tayor yat tu tat kartā labhate phalam
english: After death a man obtains the fruit of good and evil, with the elements as his witnesses; and whichever of the two preponderates, that is the fruit the doer reaps.

sanskrit: tasmād dānena tapasā karmaṇā ca śubhaṃ phalam vardhayed aśubhaṃ kṛtvā yathā syād atirekavān
english: Therefore, when he has done an evil deed, let him by gift, by austerity, and by good works so increase the fruit of merit that it comes to outweigh the rest.

sanskrit: kuryāc chubhāni karmāṇi nimitte pāpakarmaṇām dadyān nityaṃ ca vittāni tathā mucyeta kilbiṣāt
english: As an antidote to evil deeds he should perform good works, and give away his wealth without ceasing; thus he is released from sin.

sanskrit: anurūpaṃ hi pāpasya prāyaścittam udāhṛtam mahāpātakavarjaṃ tu prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate
english: For a penance proportioned to the sin has been laid down; yet, save for the great sins, an expiation is indeed prescribed.

sanskrit: bhakṣyābhakṣyeṣu sarveṣu vācyāvācye tathaiva ca ajñānajñānayo rājan vihitāny anujānate
english: In all matters of what may and may not be eaten, and likewise of what may and may not be spoken, in cases of ignorance and of knowledge alike, O king, the ordinances grant their dispensations.

sanskrit: jānatā tu kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ guru sarvaṃ bhavaty uta ajñānāt skhalite doṣe prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate
english: A sin done knowingly becomes in every case a grave one; but where the fault arises from a lapse made in ignorance, expiation is ordained.

sanskrit: śakyate vidhinā pāpaṃ yathoktena vyapohitum āstike śraddadhāne tu vidhir eṣa vidhīyate
english: Sin can be wiped away by the procedure as it has been declared; but this procedure is ordained only for the believer who has faith.

sanskrit: nāstikāśraddadhāneṣu puruṣeṣu kadā cana dambhadoṣapradhāneṣu vidhir eṣa na dṛśyate
english: For unbelieving men, devoid of faith and given over to the vice of hypocrisy, this procedure is never to be seen at all.

sanskrit: śiṣṭācāraś ca śiṣṭaś ca dharmo dharmabhṛtāṃ vara sevitavyo naravyāghra pretya ceha sukhārthinā
english: The conduct of the cultivated and the dharma the cultivated uphold, O best of the upholders of dharma, must be honored, O tiger among men, by one who seeks happiness both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: sa rājan mokṣyase pāpāt tena pūrveṇa hetunā trāṇārthaṃ vā vadhenaiṣām atha vā nṛpakarmaṇā
english: Thus, O king, you shall be freed of sin by that cause already stated, whether by reason of the slaying of these men for the protection of others, or by reason of a king's proper duty.

sanskrit: atha vā te ghṛṇā kā cit prāyaścittaṃ cariṣyasi mā tv evānāryajuṣṭena karmaṇā nidhanaṃ gamaḥ
english: Or, if some compassion still remains in you, you may perform a penance; but do not go to your ruin through conduct fit only for the ignoble.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukto bhagavatā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ tu pratyuvāca tapodhanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the venerable one, Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of dharma, reflected for a moment and then replied to the sage whose wealth was austerity.

sanskrit: kiṃ bhakṣyaṃ kim abhakṣyaṃ ca kiṃ ca deyaṃ praśasyate kiṃ ca pātram apātraṃ vā tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: What is to be eaten and what is not to be eaten, and what gift is held praiseworthy, and who is a worthy recipient and who is not — tell me this, O grandsire.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam siddhānāṃ caiva saṃvādaṃ manoś caiva prajāpateḥ
english: Vyāsa said: On this point too they relate an ancient tale, the dialogue between the Siddhas and Manu, the Lord of Creatures.

sanskrit: siddhās tapovrataparāḥ samāgamya purā vibhum dharmaṃ papracchur āsīnam ādikāle prajāpatim
english: In the days of old the Siddhas, devoted to austerity and vows, having come together, questioned about dharma the mighty Lord of Creatures as he sat there at the beginning of time.

sanskrit: katham annaṃ kathaṃ dānaṃ katham adhyayanaṃ tapaḥ kāryākāryaṃ ca naḥ sarvaṃ śaṃsa vai tvaṃ prajāpate
english: How is one to eat, how to give, how to study, how to practice austerity? Declare to us all, O Lord of Creatures, what ought and what ought not to be done.

sanskrit: tair evam ukto bhagavān manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt śuśrūṣadhvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ dharmaṃ vyāsasamāsataḥ
english: Thus addressed by them, the venerable Manu, son of the Self-Existent, replied: Listen, as it truly is, to dharma told both in full and in brief.

sanskrit: adattasyānupādānaṃ dānam adhyayanaṃ tapaḥ ahiṃsā satyam akrodhaḥ kṣamejyā dharmalakṣaṇam
english: Not taking what is not given, giving, study, austerity, non-injury, truthfulness, freedom from anger, forbearance, and sacrifice — these are the marks of dharma.

sanskrit: ya eva dharmaḥ so 'dharmo 'deśe 'kāle pratiṣṭhitaḥ ādānam anṛtaṃ hiṃsā dharmo vyāvasthikaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: That very thing which is dharma becomes unrighteousness when set in the wrong place or the wrong time; even taking, falsehood, and injury may be dharma — for dharma, it is taught, is conditioned by circumstance.

sanskrit: dvividhau cāpy ubhāv etau dharmādharmau vijānatām apravṛttiḥ pravṛttiś ca dvaividhyaṃ lokavedayoḥ
english: For those who understand, both dharma and its opposite are twofold; abstention from action and engagement in action — such is the twofold division both in worldly life and in the Veda.

sanskrit: apravṛtter amartyatvaṃ martyatvaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam aśubhasyāśubhaṃ vidyāc chubhasya śubham eva ca
english: From abstention comes immortality, while mortality is the fruit of action; one should know that the fruit of evil is evil, and that of good is good alone.

sanskrit: etayoś cobhayoḥ syātāṃ śubhāśubhatayā tathā daivaṃ ca daivayuktaṃ ca prāṇaś ca pralayaś ca ha
english: Of these two there exist, according to their good and evil nature, both the divine and what is joined to the divine, both the breath of life and dissolution.

sanskrit: aprekṣāpūrvakaraṇād aśubhānāṃ śubhaṃ phalam ūrdhvaṃ bhavati saṃdehād iha dṛṣṭārtham eva vā aprekṣāpūrvakaraṇāt prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate
english: When evil deeds are done without forethought, a good fruit may yet arise hereafter, in doubtful measure, or even for a purpose seen in this world; and for what is done without forethought an expiation is ordained.

sanskrit: krodhamohakṛte caiva dṛṣṭāntāgamahetubhiḥ śarīrāṇām upakleśo manasaś ca priyāpriye tad auṣadhaiś ca mantraiś ca prāyaścittaiś ca śāmyati
english: As for deeds done in anger and delusion — by precedent, scripture, and reason it is shown that the affliction of the body and of the mind, in things pleasant and unpleasant, is quieted by medicines, by sacred formulas, and by penances.

sanskrit: jātiśreṇyadhivāsānāṃ kuladharmāṃś ca sarvataḥ varjayen na hi taṃ dharmaṃ yeṣāṃ dharmo na vidyate
english: The customs of castes, of guilds, and of settlements, and the laws of families in every respect, one should not forsake; for there is no dharma among those in whom dharma is not found.

sanskrit: daśa vā vedaśāstrajñās trayo vā dharmapāṭhakāḥ yad brūyuḥ kārya utpanne sa dharmo dharmasaṃśaye
english: What ten men learned in the Vedas and the law-books, or three who are reciters of dharma, declare when a matter arises — that is dharma in a case of doubt concerning dharma.

sanskrit: aruṇā mṛttikā caiva tathā caiva pipīlakāḥ śleṣmātakas tathā viprair abhakṣyaṃ viṣam eva ca
english: Red earth, and likewise ants, and the śleṣmātaka fruit, and poison too — these are not to be eaten by the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: abhakṣyā brāhmaṇair matsyāḥ śakalair ye vivarjitāḥ catuṣpāt kacchapād anyo maṇḍūkā jalajāś ca ye
english: Not to be eaten by Brāhmaṇas are those fishes that are without scales, four-footed creatures other than the tortoise, frogs, and whatever else is born of the water.

sanskrit: bhāsā haṃsāḥ suparṇāś ca cakravākā bakāḥ plavāḥ kaṅko madguś ca gṛdhrāś ca kākolūkaṃ tathaiva ca
english: Bhāsa birds, swans, eagles, cakravāka geese, cranes, waterfowl, the heron, the diver-bird, vultures, and crows and owls as well —

sanskrit: kravyādāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarve catuṣpādāś ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ yeṣāṃ cobhayato dantāś caturdaṃṣṭrāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: all flesh-eating birds, and four-footed beasts furnished with fangs, those that have teeth on both jaws, and all that have the four canine teeth —

sanskrit: eḍakāśvakharoṣṭrīṇāṃ sūtikānāṃ gavām api mānuṣīṇāṃ mṛgīṇāṃ ca na pibed brāhmaṇaḥ payaḥ
english: the milk of ewes, mares, she-asses, and she-camels, of cows newly calved, and of women and of doe-deer as well — of these the Brāhmaṇa should not drink.

sanskrit: pretānnaṃ sūtikānnaṃ ca yac ca kiṃ cid anirdaśam abhojyaṃ cāpy apeyaṃ ca dhenvā dugdham anirdaśam
english: Food connected with a death, food connected with childbirth, and whatever has not yet passed its tenth day, is not to be eaten nor drunk; so too the milk of a cow within ten days of calving.

sanskrit: takṣṇaś carmāvakartuś ca puṃś calyā rajakasya ca cikitsakasya yac cānnam abhojyaṃ rakṣiṇas tathā
english: The food of a carpenter, of a tanner of hides, of an unchaste woman, of a washerman, of a physician, and likewise of a watchman, is not to be eaten.

sanskrit: gaṇagrāmābhiśastānāṃ raṅgastrījīvinaś ca ye parivittinapuṃṣāṃ ca bandidyūtavidāṃ tathā
english: So too the food of those denounced by guilds or villages, of those who live off women of the stage, of a younger brother married before the elder and of eunuchs, and of bards and those skilled in dicing —

sanskrit: vāryamāṇāhṛtaṃ cānnaṃ śuktaṃ paryuṣitaṃ ca yat surānugatam ucchiṣṭam abhojyaṃ śeṣitaṃ ca yat
english: and food brought though it was being refused, food that has soured or gone stale, food tainted with liquor, defiled leavings, and whatever has been left as a remnant — all this is not to be eaten.

sanskrit: piṣṭamāṃsekṣuśākānāṃ vikārāḥ payasas tathā saktudhānākarambhāś ca nopabhojyāś cirasthitāḥ
english: Preparations of flour, of meat, of sugarcane, of greens, and likewise of milk, and barley-meal, parched grain, and gruel of curds and meal, are not to be eaten when they have stood long.

sanskrit: pāyasaṃ kṛsaraṃ māṃsam apūpāś ca vṛthā kṛtāḥ abhojyāś cāpy abhakṣyāś ca brāhmaṇair gṛhamedhibhiḥ
english: Milk-rice, a dish of rice and sesame, meat, and cakes prepared to no sacred purpose, are not to be eaten nor partaken of by Brāhmaṇa householders.

sanskrit: devān pitṝn manuṣyāṃś ca munīn gṛhyāś ca devatāḥ pūjayitvā tataḥ paścād gṛhastho bhoktum arhati
english: Only after he has honored the gods, the ancestors, men, the sages, and the household deities is the householder entitled to eat.

sanskrit: yathā pravrajito bhikṣur gṛhasthaḥ svagṛhe vaset evaṃvṛttaḥ priyair dāraiḥ saṃvasan dharmam āpnuyāt
english: As a mendicant who has gone forth, so should the householder dwell within his own home; living thus, abiding with his beloved wife, he attains to dharma.

sanskrit: na dadyād yaśase dānaṃ na bhayān nopakāriṇe na nṛttagītaśīleṣu hāsakeṣu ca dhārmikaḥ
english: The righteous man should not give a gift for the sake of fame, nor out of fear, nor to one who has done him a service, nor to those given to dancing and singing, nor to jesters.

sanskrit: na matte naiva conmatte na stene na cikitsake na vāgghīne vivarṇe vā nāṅgahīne na vāmane
english: Not to a drunkard, nor to a madman, nor to a thief, nor to a physician, nor to one bereft of speech or pallid, nor to one maimed in limb, nor to a dwarf —

sanskrit: na durjane dauṣkule vā vratair vā yo na saṃskṛtaḥ aśrotriye mṛtaṃ dānaṃ brāhmaṇe 'brahmavādini
english: nor to a wicked man, nor to one of base family, nor to one not consecrated by the vows; a gift to a Brāhmaṇa unlearned in scripture, who does not expound the sacred word, is a gift that is dead.

sanskrit: asamyak caiva yad dattam asamyak ca pratigrahaḥ ubhayoḥ syād anarthāya dātur ādātur eva ca
english: What is given improperly, and what is improperly received, turns to the ruin of them both — of the giver and of the taker alike.

sanskrit: yathā khadiram ālambya śilāṃ vāpy arṇavaṃ taran majjate majjate tadvad dātā yaś ca pratīcchakaḥ
english: As a man who would cross the sea clinging to a log of khadira wood or to a stone sinks down, so do both the giver and the receiver sink alike.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhair ārdrair yathā vahnir upastīrṇo na dīpyate tapaḥsvādhyāyacāritrair evaṃ hīnaḥ pratigrahī
english: As a fire heaped over with damp wood does not blaze up, so is the recipient of gifts who is devoid of austerity, of study of the scriptures, and of good conduct.

sanskrit: kapāle yadvad āpaḥ syuḥ śvadṛtau vā yathā payaḥ āśrayasthānadoṣeṇa vṛttahīne tathā śrutam
english: As water held in a skull, or as milk in a dog-skin bag, is spoiled by the fault of its vessel, so is sacred learning in one bereft of good conduct.

sanskrit: nirmantro nirvrato yaḥ syād aśāstrajño 'nasūyakaḥ anukrośāt pradātavyaṃ dīneṣv evaṃ nareṣv api
english: To one who is without sacred formulas, without vows, ignorant of the scriptures, yet free of malice — out of compassion a gift may be given, even to such poor men as these.

sanskrit: na vai deyam anukrośād dīnāyāpy apakāriṇe āptācaritam ity eva dharma ity eva vā punaḥ
english: Yet a gift should not be given even out of compassion to a wretch who works harm — neither on the plea that the worthy have practiced it, nor again on the plea that it is dharma.

sanskrit: niṣkāraṇaṃ sma tad dattaṃ brāhmaṇe dharmavarjite bhaved apātradoṣeṇa na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: A gift made without good cause to a Brāhmaṇa devoid of dharma incurs the fault of an unworthy recipient — on this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: yathā dārumayo hastī yathā carmamayo mṛgaḥ brāhmaṇaś cānadhīyānas trayas te nāmadhārakāḥ
english: As an elephant made of wood, as a deer made of leather, so too a Brāhmaṇa who does not study — these three bear but the name.

sanskrit: yathā ṣaṇḍho 'phalaḥ strīṣu yathā gaur gavi cāphalā śakunir vāpy apakṣaḥ syān nirmantro brāhmaṇas tathā
english: As a eunuch is barren among women, as a cow with a cow yields no fruit, as a bird without wings — so is a Brāhmaṇa without the sacred formulas.

sanskrit: grāmadhānyaṃ yathā śūnyaṃ yathā kūpaś ca nirjalaḥ yathā hutam anagnau ca tathaiva syān nirākṛtau
english: As grain stored in an empty village, as a well without water, as an oblation poured where there is no fire — even so is an offering made to one untrained in sacred rites.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca havyakavyavināśanaḥ śatrur arthaharo mūrkho na lokān prāptum arhati
english: A fool who destroys the offerings due to the gods and the ancestors, an enemy who carries off their substance, does not deserve to attain the higher worlds.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yathā vṛttaṃ yudhiṣṭhira samāsena mahad dhy etac chrotavyaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: All this has been told to you as it truly came to pass, O Yudhiṣṭhira; in brief it has been declared, yet it is a great matter to be heard, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrotum icchāmi bhagavan vistareṇa mahāmune rājadharmān dvijaśreṣṭha cāturvarṇyasya cākhilān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I wish to hear at length, O venerable one, O great sage, O best of the twice-born, the whole of the duties of kings and of all the four castes.

sanskrit: āpatsu ca yathā nītir vidhātavyā mahīkṣitā dharmyam ālambya panthānaṃ vijayeyaṃ kathaṃ mahīm
english: And how, in times of calamity, statecraft is to be ordered by a ruler of the earth, and how, keeping to the path of righteousness, I might win the whole earth.

sanskrit: prāyaścittakathā hy eṣā bhakṣyābhakṣyavivardhitā kautūhalānupravaṇā harṣaṃ janayatīva me
english: For this discourse on expiation, enlarged with the matter of foods lawful and forbidden, has stirred my curiosity and seems to awaken delight in me.

sanskrit: dharmacaryā ca rājyaṃ ca nityam eva virudhyate yena muhyati me cetaś cintayānasya nityaśaḥ
english: The practice of dharma and the rule of a kingdom seem forever at war with one another, and by this my mind is confounded as I ponder it without cease.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tam uvāca mahātejā vyāso vedavidāṃ varaḥ nāradaṃ samabhiprekṣya sarvaṃ jānan purātanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To him the mighty Vyāsa, best of those who know the Vedas, who knew all that was of old, glancing toward Nārada, spoke.

sanskrit: śrotum icchasi ced dharmān akhilena yudhiṣṭhira praihi bhīṣmaṃ mahābāho vṛddhaṃ kurupitāmaham
english: If you wish to hear the whole of dharma, O Yudhiṣṭhira, go forth, O mighty-armed one, to Bhīṣma, the aged grandsire of the Kurus.

sanskrit: sa te sarvarahasyeṣu saṃśayān manasi sthitān chettā bhāgīrathīputraḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvadharmavit
english: In all the mysteries he will cut away the doubts that abide in your mind — the son of Bhāgīrathī, the all-knowing, the knower of all dharma.

sanskrit: janayām āsa yaṃ devī divyā tripathagā nadī sākṣād dadarśa yo devān sarvāñ śakrapurogamān
english: He whom the divine goddess, the celestial river that flows by three paths, brought to birth; he who beheld face to face all the gods with Śakra at their head.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatipurogāṃś ca devarṣīn asakṛt prabhuḥ toṣayitvopacāreṇa rājanītim adhītavān
english: Having again and again gratified with due homage the divine seers, with Bṛhaspati at their head, the lord learned the science of statecraft.

sanskrit: uśanā veda yac chāstraṃ devāsuragurur dvijaḥ tac ca sarvaṃ savaiyākhyaṃ prāptavān kurusattamaḥ
english: That whole science which the Brāhmaṇa Uśanas, preceptor of gods and demons, knows, this best of the Kurus obtained together with all its commentary.

sanskrit: bhārgavāc cyavanāc cāpi vedān aṅgopabṛṃhitān pratipede mahābuddhir vasiṣṭhāc ca yatavratāt
english: From Cyavana of the Bhārgava line the great-minded one received the Vedas with their supplementary limbs, and also from Vasiṣṭha, firm in his vows.

sanskrit: pitāmahasutaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ kumāraṃ dīptatejasam adhyātmagatitattvajñam upāśikṣata yaḥ purā
english: He who of old learned from the eldest son of the grandsire, the youth of blazing splendor, who knew the true nature of the path of the inmost Self.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeyamukhāt kṛtsnaṃ yatidharmam avāptavān rāmād astrāṇi śakrāc ca prāptavān bharatarṣabha
english: From the mouth of Mārkaṇḍeya he gained the whole law of the ascetics, and from Rāma weapons, and from Śakra he obtained them too, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: mṛtyur ātmecchayā yasya jātasya manujeṣv api tathānapatyasya sataḥ puṇyalokā divi śrutāḥ
english: He whose death, though born among men, comes only by his own will; and though he is without offspring, the holy worlds in heaven are said to be his.

sanskrit: yasya brahmarṣayaḥ puṇyā nityam āsan sabhāsadaḥ yasya nāviditaṃ kiṃ cij jñānajñeyeṣu vidyate
english: He in whose assembly the holy Brāhmaṇa-seers ever sat as members; for whom nothing whatever among the things to be known by knowledge remains unknown.

sanskrit: sa te vakṣyati dharmajñaḥ sūkṣmadharmārthatattvavit tam abhyehi purā prāṇān sa vimuñcati dharmavit
english: He, the knower of dharma, versed in the subtle truth of dharma and of its purport, will declare it to you; go to him before that knower of dharma releases his life-breaths.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kaunteyo dīrghaprajño mahādyutiḥ uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vyāsaṃ satyavatīsutam
english: Thus addressed, the son of Kuntī, far-sighted in wisdom and of great splendor, spoke to Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī, best of those who speak.

sanskrit: vaiśasaṃ sumahat kṛtvā jñātīnāṃ lomaharṣaṇam āgaskṛt sarvalokasya pṛthivīnāśakārakaḥ
english: Having wrought a most terrible carnage of my kinsmen, one that makes the hair stand on end, having become a sinner against the whole world and the cause of the earth's ruin —

sanskrit: ghātayitvā tam evājau chalenājihmayodhinam upasaṃpraṣṭum arhāmi tam ahaṃ kena hetunā
english: having caused him to be slain in battle by guile, though he fought without crookedness — by what right am I fit to approach him with my questions?

sanskrit: tatas taṃ nṛpatiśreṣṭhaṃ cāturvarṇyahitepsayā punar āha mahābāhur yaduśreṣṭho mahādyutiḥ
english: Then, desiring the welfare of the four castes, the mighty-armed one of great splendor, best of the Yadus, spoke again to that best of kings.
